basis: Ectodermal dysplasia, renal defects and lipoatrophic diabetes define disease; sideroblastic anemia 80-99%; skeletal and dental abnormalities also 80-99%, omitted by cap.
Primary immunodeficiency; recurrent infections are separate diseases. Frequencies of bronchiectasis and intellectual disability are insufficiently established here.
Immune-mediated dural inflammation and thickening; ocular, renal, pulmonary and pancreatic manifestations are each reported in only 5-29%.
Seizures, profound intellectual disability and developmental delay in 9/9; feeding support reflects neurologic dysfunction; scoliosis only 2/9.
Defined as a hereditary neurodevelopmental and movement disorder; the enzyme's metabolic role alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Inherited disorder of skin cornification; additional organ damage is not established across most patients in this umbrella group.
Benign tumor of the nasal cavity, which belongs to the upper respiratory tract.
Renal tubular electrolyte-handling disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and hypertension.
Benign fibroblastic tumor arising in the lung.
Peroxisomal metabolic disease with neurologic dysfunction; hepatopathy and retinal degeneration are common (>30%) across Zellweger spectrum; hearing loss omitted by cap.
Renal lesions in 80-99%; cardiac rhabdomyomas in 30-79% and a major criterion. Retinal hamartomas and pulmonary lymphangioleiomyomatosis omitted by cap.
Autoinflammatory syndrome; recurrent fever alone does not establish lasting damage to another organ across the umbrella group.
Congenital cardiac and limb malformations define the embryofetopathy; VSD and clinodactyly 80-99%. Hypertrichosis resolves; other organ frequencies uncertain.
Inhaled silica directly causes pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis; associated infections and autoimmune diseases are separate diagnoses.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with focal segmental glomerular scarring; an immune mechanism is not established for this heterogeneous entity.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across partial chromosome 2 duplications; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
Benign wart-like epithelial papilloma; dermatologic assignment is provisional because the anatomical site is unspecified. An infectious cause is not established.
Malignant tumor arising in the external, middle or inner ear.
Defined by skeletal malformations and oral anomalies, including polysyndactyly, brachymesophalangy, cleft lip and accessory oral frenula.
Quantitative von Willebrand factor deficiency causes a coagulation disorder; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish separate organ damage.
Congenital bilateral duplication of a biphalangeal thumb.
Bladder outlet dysfunction with retention and structural bladder changes; neurologic deficits are absent. Recurrent UTIs are separate infections.
Congenital vertebral fusion; hearing impairment 20/24 (~83%) and renal anomalies 16/45 (~36%); neurologic anomalies 5/19 (~26%) excluded.
Familial focal epilepsy, often associated with focal cortical dysplasia; no common direct extra-neurologic organ damage is established.
